The gray small rectangle is composed of three identical squares arranged side by side. According to the specified labels, the four vertices of the gray small rectangle are A = upper left, B = upper right, C = lower right, D = lower left. In the figure, D and B respectively lie on the two shorter sides of the larger rectangle, and the problem statement says that they are the midpoints of these two short sides; A and C respectively lie on the other two sides of the larger rectangle. Then reason: The area of each small square is 25 cm², so the side length is 5 cm. Therefore the dimensions of the internal small rectangle are 15 cm × 5 cm. Take coordinates D=(0,0), A=(0,5), C=(15,0), B=(15,5). Because D and B are the midpoints of the two short sides of the larger rectangle, DB is the line segment connecting the midpoints of the two short sides, and in the rectangle it is parallel to the long side, and its length is equal to the length of the large rectangle. Thus the length of the large rectangle is |DB| = sqrt(15²+5²)=sqrt(250)=5sqrt(10). The width of the large rectangle is the perpendicular distance between the two long sides passing through A and through C, and both parallel to DB. Using the vector cross product to calculate, DB=(15,5), AC=(15,-5), distance = |DB × AC| / |DB| = |15(-5)-5(15)|/(5sqrt(10)) = 150/(5sqrt(10)) = 3sqrt(10). Therefore the area of the large rectangle = (5sqrt(10))(3sqrt(10)) = 150.

The gray small rectangle is composed of three identical squares arranged side by side. According to the specified labels, the four vertices of the gray small rectangle are A = upper left, B = upper right, C = lower right, D = lower left. In the figure, D and B respectively lie on the two shorter sides of the larger rectangle, and the problem statement says that they are the midpoints of these two short sides; A and C respectively lie on the other two sides of the larger rectangle.

Then reason: The area of each small square is 25 cm², so the side length is 5 cm. Therefore the dimensions of the internal small rectangle are 15 cm × 5 cm. Take coordinates D=(0,0), A=(0,5), C=(15,0), B=(15,5). Because D and B are the midpoints of the two short sides of the larger rectangle, DB is the line segment connecting the midpoints of the two short sides, and in the rectangle it is parallel to the long side, and its length is equal to the length of the large rectangle.

Thus the length of the large rectangle is |DB| = sqrt(15²+5²)=sqrt(250)=5sqrt(10). The width of the large rectangle is the perpendicular distance between the two long sides passing through A and through C, and both parallel to DB. Using the vector cross product to calculate, DB=(15,5), AC=(15,-5), distance = |DB × AC| / |DB| = |15(-5)-5(15)|/(5sqrt(10)) = 150/(5sqrt(10)) = 3sqrt(10).

Therefore the area of the large rectangle = (5sqrt(10))(3sqrt(10)) = 150.
